newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn to sell oil reserves in 1997 and 1998 - source.
newsitem.headline: Bonn to sell oil reserves in 1997 and 1998 - source.

text.p: Government sources said on Friday that Germany expected to raise around 400 million marks ($230 million) in revenue this year from the sale of a part of its oil reserves.
The sources added that further oil sales would take place next year, but did not say how much oil Germany would sell in 1998 or how much revenue it expected to gain.
German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said last month the government was considering selling 7.3 million tonnes from its oil reserves and that this would raise around 1.4 billion marks.
The government said at the time that this was just one of the measures it was considering as a way to plug yawning budget deficits as it struggles to qualify for European monetary union.
Other measures include stepped up privatisations such as the early sale of more of the government's stake in phone monnopoly Deutsche Telekom AG.
The budget deficit is now expected to surge to 71 billion marks this year, up from an original plan of 53.3 billion, and to fall back to just under 58 billion marks next year.
